settings.browserHint: Launches a Chromium browser with --proxy-server (so mitmproxy captures the traffic), --remote-debugging-port (so bookmarks can read the active tab), and a project-local profile so these flags never touch your daily browsing.
settings.httpCapturePortHint: Loopback browser proxy URLs use this port. Remote/custom proxy URLs remain external and are not managed by RedLog.
settings.httpCaptureHostHint: Where the capture proxy binds. 127.0.0.1 keeps it on this machine. Widen it to point a victim VM, a phone, a container or a NAT’d WSL distro at the capture.
settings.httpCaptureExposedWarning: Bound to {{host}}: anything that can reach this address can use RedLog as an open proxy, and its traffic lands in your evidence. Only do this on a network you control.
settings.browserIgnoreCert: Ignore certificate errors (needed for mitmproxy interception)
settings.browserNotFound: No Chromium-based browser found — set a path above
settings.displayZoneHint: Every event time in the app is printed in this zone, and a UTC time ends in Z. Exports stay ISO 8601 with the offset.
settings.agents.hint: Watches AI-coding-agent transcript files and derives per-turn audit events into the hash chain. Off means no agent conversation, tool call, or response is captured — the sidecar files stay untouched.
settings.agents.enableHint: Off by default. When enabled, watches supported agent transcript locations; use the path allowlist below to limit capture to engagement directories.
settings.agents.emitThinkingHint: Emits `agent.thinking` events for assistant reasoning blocks. Off by default — blocks are large and mostly meta. Turn on for AI-safety red-team or tool-use policy audits.
settings.agents.selfExclusionHint: A `.redlog-app-root` marker file in a project cwd opts that repo out of tailing — used to prevent RedLog watching its own dev sessions. Commit the marker to any repo you don't want tailed.
settings.name: Name
settings.whitelist: Safe IPs — where it's OK to attack from (VPN/VPS exits). External IP matching → SAFE (green).
settings.blacklist: Exposed IPs — your own fixed IPs (home ISP, office). External IP matching → EXPOSED (red, identity leak).
settings.ipModeHint: How the external IP is fetched. DNS is quieter and not rate-limited but can be blocked on restrictive networks; Auto tries DNS first, then HTTP.
settings.showWifiNameHint: macOS hides the Wi-Fi SSID behind Location Services. Enabling this asks for permission once so the HUD can show the real network name instead of a generic "Wi-Fi". Location data never leaves your machine.
settings.pollingOpsecHint: Each poll is an outbound request to a third party from the operator's box. At 10s that is ~8,600 requests a day — a periodic beacon a defender can fingerprint. 60s or more is a safer default; point the providers below at your own endpoint to avoid third parties entirely.
settings.confirmations: Readings required before the address changes
settings.confirmationsHint: Egress behind CGNAT or a load-balanced pool answers differently each poll. Requiring several identical reads stops the safety badge flickering between SAFE and EXPOSED.
settings.ipProvidersHint: Tried in order until one answers. Must return JSON with an "ip" field.
settings.vpnAdaptersHint: Which VPN adapter names to look for when checking whether a tunnel is up. Toggle built-in presets or add custom patterns (case-insensitive regex matched against the interface name).
settings.overlayShowMark: Show Mark button in the expanded overlay
settings.overlayShowMarkHint: Keeps the collapsed overlay minimal; the Mark button only appears when expanded.
settings.overlayFlashExposedHint: When the external IP hits the blacklist (EXPOSED), flash the whole HUD frame red so it's hard to miss. Off leaves just the red status dot pulsing.
settings.overlayScaleHint: Scales every font size + padding together; the window auto-resizes to fit.
settings.overlayEmphasizeIpHint: Bumps the external IP an extra ~1.4× on top of the overall scale, so an OPSEC glance always lands on it first.
settings.overlayPassThroughHint: The HUD stops receiving clicks — stray drags won't steal focus from Burp / a browser sitting under it. Opacity drops so you can see it's non-interactive. Exit with ⌘⇧P or the menu bar.
settings.clipboardEnableHint: Records the moment a credential/token was copied. Content is run through loot detection + redaction; only SHA-256, length, line count and matched credential types are stored. Raw text never lands. Detected credentials get their own loot event.
settings.clipboardStorePreviewHint: Keep a redacted preview alongside the hash for later cross-reference. Leave off if you're worried about redaction gaps.
settings.fileWatcherEnableHint: Emits file_transfer events when files in the watched paths are created/modified/deleted. node_modules/, .git/, dist/, out/, build/, .DS_Store and editor temp files are ignored by default.
settings.fileWatcherIgnoreHint: Gitignore-style globs on top of the built-in defaults. One per line.
settings.processMonitorEnableHint: Polls ps every 500ms; emits process_spawn / process_exit events for the new lane. Windows is not supported yet. RedLog's own processes are ignored automatically.
settings.processMonitorIgnoreHint: Match by leading token (first word or basename). Case-sensitive.
settings.overlayShowInDockHint: Opening the HUD otherwise makes RedLog Dock-less. Off = run from the menu bar / HUD only, no Dock icon.
settings.screenshot.intervalHint: Auto-capture the desktop at the chosen cadence. Identical frames are deduped by SHA-256 so an idle screen doesn't spam the chain.
settings.rotationHint: Per-store size budgets in MB. 0 = keep everything (no eviction). When a store exceeds its budget the coldest out-of-scope files are evicted first; files whose target is in the engagement scope are pinned and kept. The event and its SHA-256 always survive — only the on-disk file is dropped.
settings.retentionLoggedTier: Traffic events (HTTP / DNS / process) keep days
settings.retentionLoggedTierHint: Days to keep logged-tier rows (HTTP flows, DNS, process spawn). 0 = keep forever. These rows are not hash-chained; they serve as investigative context.
settings.checkUpdateHint: Checks GitHub for a newer release. RedLog also checks automatically at launch.
settings.qualityHint: Higher = better quality, larger files. Default: 85
settings.screenshot.diffLabel: Differential capture (store only on visible change)
settings.screenshot.diffHint: For periodic/idle captures only — a frame that looks the same as the last stored one (perceptual dHash) is skipped, so an idle screen doesn't fill the store. Manual captures always land. "Every frame" disables the skip; "Major changes only" needs a bigger change to store.
settings.screenshot.onCommandHint: Capture a frame on each shell command_end, linked to that command, so a report can pair "command → resulting screen". Best for GUI-heavy work (Burp, a browser); a command that changed nothing visible is skipped by the diff above, and terminal output is better read from the .cast recording.
settings.warnOnViolationHint: When a command's target is outside scope but shares a root domain with a scope target, raise a red badge + scope_violation event. Excluded targets always warn regardless. RedLog only records — it never blocks a command.
settings.personalDomainsHint: Hosts that are never part of any engagement — personal browsing, localhost, update CDNs. Matched rows are dropped entirely on export (not masked). Same syntax: IP, CIDR, *.domain.
settings.scopeFileLabel: Load targets from file (JSON or plain text, one per line)
settings.scopeFileHint: Absolute path to a scope file. Targets are merged with the list above.
settings.autoSaveHint: Changes save automatically and apply live (changing engagement/operator id needs reopening the project)
settings.hookWatchPaths.title: Claude Code Hook — Watch Paths
settings.hookWatchPaths.hint: Only Claude Code sessions whose working directory matches a path listed here will be logged. If the list is empty, all sessions are logged. Add your engagement's working directory to scope capture.
settings.hookWatchPaths.empty: No watch paths — all Claude Code sessions are logged. Add your project directory to scope capture.
settings.integrityHint: The event chain is anchored to public OpenTimestamps calendars every hour. Each receipt lets any auditor prove the chain existed at that time — verifiable independently with the `ots` CLI.
settings.integrityNoAnchors: No anchors yet. Click Anchor now to submit the current chain head.

This is not an OS sandbox. Only trust plugins whose source you trust.
plugins.consentWarn: Trust is pinned to the plugin's current code. If the code changes, trust is revoked until you review it again.

screenshots.deleteFailed: Could not delete the image file
screenshots.deleteFailedWhy: The event stays in the chain either way — only the JPEG was going to be removed.
capture.actionFailedWhy: The hook was not changed. The shell profile may be read-only, or the path no longer exists.
transcript.copyFailedWhy: The clipboard refused the write. Another application may be holding it.
project.openMissingWhy: The folder is gone or on a volume that is not mounted.
confirm.ackDefault: I understand this cannot be undone.
settings.cdpNotConnectedTitle: Chrome is not answering on the debugging port
settings.hookFailedWhy: The shell profile was not written. It may be read-only, or the path in Settings no longer exists.
plugins.grantFailedWhy: The plugin stays unable to run. Its manifest may have changed since it was installed.
settings.anchorFailedWhy: Events keep being chained, but nothing timestamps them externally until an anchor lands. Check network access and retry.
settings.integrityNoAnchorsWhy: There is nothing to anchor yet — the chain is empty.
project.openFailedWhy: Nothing was changed or loaded. The database may be locked by another RedLog window.
timeline.saveFailedWhy: Your text is still in the field — copy it before closing the panel.
terminal.tabClosedWhy: The shell process ended. Undo opens a new one — scrollback does not come back.
toast.recordingPausedWhy: Capture sources stop feeding the timeline. Your markers and RedLog’s own audit events keep recording.
plugins.disabledWhy: Not written yet — undo within 8 seconds and nothing reaches the audit log.
targets.addedToScopeWhy: Not written yet — undo within 8 seconds and nothing reaches the audit log.
settings.hookRemovedWhy: Not written yet — undo within 8 seconds and the profile is never touched.
issues.captureDetail: Events are still being written, but at least one source has stopped producing — the gap will be in the timeline, not in an error.
issues.chainBroken: The evidence chain does not verify
issues.chainBrokenDetail: A row between the anchor and now does not hash to its successor. Export a bundle before doing anything else.
issues.chainAnchorMismatchDetail: Every row hashes to its successor, but the chain no longer matches its latest anchor: it was rewritten or cut short after it was anchored. Export a bundle before doing anything else.
fatal.title: {{view}} stopped working
fatal.why: Nothing has been lost — events already recorded are on disk and the chain is intact. Only this view stopped rendering.
fatal.scrubbed: Paths are reduced to the app bundle, and your username and project name are replaced. Read it before sending — this is exactly what gets shared.

confirm.deleteProjectMedia: All screenshots and terminal session recordings
confirm.deleteProjectAnchors: The OpenTimestamps receipts — these cannot be regenerated, because they attest to a moment that has passed
statusBar.tierCountTitle: {{chained}} chained (the audit chain) · {{logged}} logged (supporting evidence). The filter bar's Chained only chip hides the logged rows on every view.
screenshots.emptyReason: Nothing has been captured yet, by hand or on a timer; periodic capture is off by default. Every screenshot carries a SHA-256 and the reason it was taken.
loot.emptyReason: Credentials and keys are detected in command output and clipboard content as they go past. Nothing has matched yet — which is the expected state at the start of an engagement.
targets.emptyReason: Hosts and addresses are extracted from commands, HTTP traffic and DNS queries as they are captured. Nothing has been seen yet — run something against a host and it will appear.
bookmarks.emptyReason: Bookmarks are your own browsing notes — the URL and title of the tab you are on, saved so you can come back to it. They are not evidence: not chained, not signed, editable, deletable, and not in the evidence bundle. For a finding that belongs in the record, drop a marker (⌘⇧M).
transcript.emptyReason: This is what you typed and what came back, in order. It fills from shell commands, agent turns and HTTP exchanges as they are captured.

settings.connectionMonitorSynNote: Established connections only. A SYN scan (nmap -sS) completes no handshake and will not appear — the command is still recorded, the connections are not.
timeline.detail.httpBodyEvicted: Body content no longer on disk — pruned by retention or evicted under disk pressure. The event and its SHA-256 remain; only the openable body is gone.

marker.amendErr.notFound: That marker is not here; it may belong to another project.
marker.amendErr.notAMarker: Only a marker can be amended, and an amendment cannot be amended again.
marker.amendErr.invalidChanges: Nothing in this edit can be written.

firstRun.record.waiting: Waiting for that command to arrive…
firstRun.record.timeoutTitle: Nothing arrived in 60 seconds. The most likely reasons:
firstRun.record.reasonNewTab: The shell profile was not loaded. Tabs that were already open don't pick up the hook — open a new tab and paste the command there.
firstRun.record.reasonMissing: {{names}} is missing, so the hook cannot send anything:
firstRun.record.reasonLegacy: An old RedLog hook line is still in {{file}} (line {{line}}):
firstRun.http.title: Record this engagement's HTTP(S) traffic (web testing)
firstRun.http.waiting: Waiting for the first HTTP request — open any page in the proxied browser.
firstRun.http.verified: ✓ HTTP capture verified — the first request arrived
firstRun.http.timeoutTitle: No HTTP request in 60 s. Most likely:
firstRun.http.reason.browser: Your usual browser does not use this proxy — browse in the window opened by “Open the proxied browser” above.
firstRun.http.reason.ca: The HTTPS certificate is missing or not trusted, so HTTPS sites cannot pass the proxy — see “HTTPS certificate” below.
firstRun.http.reason.terminalsOff: curl and wget in your terminals do not use the proxy — “route new terminals through this proxy” is off by default.
firstRun.http.reason.terminalsNew: Only built-in terminals opened after turning the option on use the proxy; ones already open do not.
firstRun.http.routeTerminals: Route new terminals through this proxy
firstRun.http.routeTerminalsLimit: Only affects tools that honour HTTP_PROXY (curl, wget, Python/Node HTTP clients); nmap SYN scans, SMB, LDAP and RDP do not go through this proxy.
marker.readonly.urlWhy: where the mark points; changing it changes what it points at
loot.noMatchesReason: The type filter or de-duplication is hiding every hit. Nothing was removed from the record.
settings.hookDesc.shell-zsh: Captures every command, with exit code and duration, from zsh
settings.hookDesc.shell-bash: Captures every command from bash via preexec / precmd hooks
settings.hookDesc.codex: Wraps the Codex shell so the agent's commands are captured
settings.hookDesc.mitmproxy: Captures HTTP and DNS traffic through the mitmproxy addon
settings.hookDesc.shell-powershell: Captures commands from PowerShell via a prompt hook
settings.hookDesc.shell-wsl: Captures commands from WSL bash sessions — resolves the Windows token path automatically
eventTitle.connectionCaptureOn: ⇄ Connection capture on — established connections only, no SYN scans
eventTitle.connectionSaturated: ⇄ {{count}} connections in one poll — recording the count, not each
filter.title: Filter
filter.unappliedTitle: {{condition}} is not applied on this page
filter.unappliedHttpType: HTTP History only holds the HTTP traffic the proxy recorded, so its source type is fixed. The selected type has nothing to show here, which is why the list is empty — that is not evidence the project recorded no HTTP traffic or no events of that type.
filter.unappliedTranscriptType: The Transcript only buckets these source types: {{types}}. The selected type is not one of them, so this page has nothing to show — that does not mean the project holds no events of that type.
filter.chainedOnlyHint: Show chained evidence only, the tier that is hashed and signed. Applies to every event view.
filter.chainedOnlyHttp: HTTP flows are recorded in the logged tier, so Chained only leaves nothing here. That is not evidence the project recorded no HTTP traffic.
filter.lootTypeEmpty: Loot lists only loot rows, so {{condition}} leaves nothing here. That is not evidence the project holds no events of that type.
filter.inScopeHint: Show only events targeting in-scope hosts
filter.personalHiddenHint: Hides event rows whose target matches your personal/local rules. Untargeted events and terminal recording contents are not classified. Click to show matching rows.
filter.personalShownHint: Showing rows matching your personal/local target rules. Click to hide those rows.
marker.replayAtTime.noSession: No active terminal session at this time
terminal.castTruncated: Cast recording hit size limit — output past this point is not captured
terminal.castPaused: Recording paused — this pane's output is not written while paused
terminal.castNotRecording: No cast recording for this session
query.tokenCondition: Condition: matched against the stored field
query.unparsable.empty-condition-value: “{{token}}” is a half-typed condition with no value. Give it one, or wrap it in double quotes to search for it as text.
transcript.queryToolSessionOthers: The same tool-use ID also occurs in {{count}} other session(s); add a session: condition to choose.
transcript.queryCoverage: Text search covers stored event content. Command output that was not captured inline stays in a terminal recording and cannot be matched — no hit is not evidence the output never held it.
palette.searchFailed: Event search failed — this is not the same as no matching events.
palette.searchUnparsable: That condition is incomplete (e.g. nothing after session:), so no search was run. Add a value, or quote it to search it as text.
palette.searchSubset: Newest {{count}} matches — Search lists all of them
settings.lootHint: Rules that are off are not recorded as loot. What they match is still masked in the record and in exports.
settings.lootRulesFailed: Could not load the loot rules.
statusBar.uptimeSince: Time since this project was created ({{date}}), not this session
settings.lootRuleStopped: Stopped: this rule ran past its time limit, so it no longer runs — or masks what it matches. Reload the plugin after fixing the pattern.
settings.essentialHint: Built in and not optional. Each needs its own one-time setup where noted.
settings.essentialShell: Shell commands, through the shell hook (Capture Health ▸ install)
settings.essentialHttp: HTTP(S) through mitmproxy — RedLog’s managed proxy, your own mitmproxy with RedLog’s addon, or transparent mode (Network pack). Same capture, three ways in; HTTPS needs the CA trusted.
settings.essentialPty: Full terminal output of a session started with redlog-session
settings.packRecord: Record with this pack in this project
settings.packRemoved: This pack is disabled in Plugins, so it records nothing in any project. Enable it there to use it.
settings.packHostMonitorsHint: Programs that ran, connections they held, files that changed, and what was copied — process, connection, file and clipboard monitors. Off by default.
settings.packAiAgentsHint: Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode sessions, turn by turn. Transcripts can include unrelated work, so this is off until you turn it on. Tuning is on the Agents page.
readiness.title: RedLog readiness
readiness.shellNone: not detected — use the RedLog terminal
readiness.mitmOptional: Web traffic capture needs mitmproxy; you can install it later.
readiness.legacyFound: found in {{count}} line(s) — update it from the banner
readiness.runtimeMissing: RedLog's terminal still opens and its screen output is still recorded — but no command will reach the Timeline until python3 and curl are installed. The built-in terminal sources the same adapter your own shell does.
legacyHook.message: Capture script updated: your {{file}} still loads the old RedLog hook, which records nothing after the upgrade.
legacyHook.done: Hook updated. Open a new terminal — the hook loads in new shells.
filter.listsFailed: Could not load the target and type lists. What is shown may be out of date.
filter.presetIsSnapshot: Takes a fixed window ending now — it does not keep sliding
filter.timeRangeInvalid: The end is at or before the start, so nothing can match.
readiness.checkFailed: The environment check could not run.
firstRun.readFailedWhy: This is a read failure, not an empty log — capture may well be running.
firstRun.preflightFailedTitle: The environment check could not run
firstRun.preflightFailedWhy: Missing dependencies cannot be reported until it does.
settings.save.failed: Could not save. Your changes are still here.
settings.hookRunHint: Types it into RedLog's terminal without running it — read the line, then press Enter. It is recorded like any other command.
readiness.coreReady: RedLog can record commands on this machine.
